drafts.title: Reliable voice control that understands simple driving commands
drafts.description: While driving, the driver can use natural voice commands (navigation destinations, radio/media, phone calls, and simple climate actions) and expect the system to execute the command without repeating or manual fallback.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a closed-track driving test with realistic cabin noise up to 70 dB(A), the system correctly recognizes and executes simple commands (turn-by-turn navigation destination entry, play/skip track, answer/hang up call, raise/lower temperature by 2°C) in >=90% of 1,000 evaluated utterances across at least two major languages for the market.
assumptions: Test set uses representative accents and common background noises for the target market (United States).
‘Simple commands’ are limited to navigation destination entry, media control, phone call control, and basic climate setpoints (no multi-step dialogs).
Recognition accuracy is measured end-to-end (user intent correctly interpreted and corresponding system action executed).
uncertainties: Extreme accents, very uncommon phrasings or non-supported languages may reduce accuracy.
Performance may differ between connected (cloud-assisted) and offline modes depending on connectivity at the time of test.

drafts.title: Consistent wireless phone charging that stays active while driving
drafts.description: When a Qi‑compatible phone is placed on the vehicle wireless charging pad in normal orientations and with common phone cases, it reliably charges and does not drop connection during typical trips.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In lab and real-road tests covering 10 popular Qi‑capable phone models and common cases (up to 3 mm thickness), at least 98% of charging sessions remain active for a continuous 2‑hour driving profile (including city and highway conditions) without the phone disconnecting or requiring repositioning.
assumptions: Phones tested support standard Qi charging levels used by the vehicle; tests include representative casing and alignment variability.
‘Charging session remains active’ means battery percentage increases or charging indicator remains ON for the duration of the test.
Acceptance measured across a statistically representative set of phone models for the US market.
uncertainties: Aftermarket magnetic mounts or very thick metal cases may still interfere.
Vehicle or phone firmware updates after launch can affect behavior.

drafts.title: Head-up display and center screen remain readable in bright sunlight
drafts.description: Drivers can read critical HUD information (speed, next navigation instruction) and center-screen navigation/menus in direct sunlight without needing to manually shade or change viewing angle.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In a human readability trial with ambient luminance up to 80,000 lux (direct sunlight conditions), 90% of participants can correctly identify HUD speed and next navigation turn within a 1.5 second glance and can read primary navigation content on the center screen without manual shading or repositioning.
assumptions: Trial uses standard in-vehicle seating positions and typical sunglasses (polarized and non-polarized) commonly used in the market.
Font sizes and UI contrast for tested content reflect production defaults for navigation and primary status text.
Ambient luminance test point (80,000 lux) approximates bright mid-day sunlight; different sun angles included in test matrix.
uncertainties: Extreme sun angles or unusual aftermarket window tinting may still cause readability issues.
Perception can vary with sunglasses polarization; some polarized glasses may reduce HUD visibility.

drafts.title: Tactile physical controls for temperature and fan speed that can be used without looking
drafts.description: Drivers can operate primary climate functions (temperature up/down and fan speed/preset) by touch alone, without having to look at the control stack.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In usability tests, 95% of participants can (1) change cabin temperature by at least ±2°C and (2) change between three fan speed presets using only tactile controls within 5 seconds, while seated normally and without visual feedback.
assumptions: Controls include distinct tactile features (different shapes, detents, or raised markings) so they can be differentiated by feel.
Test participants represent a cross-section of adult drivers in the target market.
Glove use and wet/dry finger conditions are represented in test variants.
uncertainties: Very small or low-profile controls may fail to meet the criterion; packaging decisions will affect feasibility.
Cultural differences in expectations for control placement may influence perceived usability in other markets.

drafts.title: Include heated steering wheel as part of the Cold Weather package
drafts.description: When customers select the Cold Weather (winter) package, the heated steering wheel is included as a bundled item rather than only as an individual paid option.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: In the vehicle configurator and order documents for target markets, the Cold Weather package includes the heated steering wheel in 100% of offered configurations and is visibly listed as part of the package contents at point of sale.
assumptions: Applies to markets where a Cold Weather package is offered; regional package content variations will be handled per market rules.
Inclusion does not specify price level — it defines package composition (heated wheel included when the Cold Weather package is selected).
uncertainties: Dealer-level aftermarket bundling or regional homologation requirements may change final package composition.
If the vehicle is offered in regions without a Cold Weather package, inclusion will not apply.

drafts.title: Request for CCC certification of the infotainment system (China)
drafts.description: Customers request that the infotainment system passes Chinese CCC certification so the vehicle can be sold/configured for China.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request logged for program and handled by regulatory/homologation team; not a product-level customer outcome.
drafts.scope_reason: This is a certification/regulatory request (homologation) and out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Request that driver profile satisfies GDPR data-storage requirements
drafts.description: Customers ask that their driver profile and related data storage follow GDPR rules and allow data control/deletion.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Request logged for legal/compliance implementation; data-protection certification and legal requirements are handled outside product feature drafts.
drafts.scope_reason: Legal/regulatory compliance (GDPR) is out of scope for product-level requirements; implement via compliance/legal workstreams.

drafts.title: Request that the cockpit computer uses the Snapdragon 8295 chip
drafts.description: Customers specifically request the vehicle use the Snapdragon 8295 chipset in the cockpit computer.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Engineering/component selection requests are recorded; chipset-level specifications are engineering decisions, not customer-facing outcomes.
drafts.scope_reason: This is an engineering/component specification request and out of scope for customer-facing product requirements.

drafts.title: Requests to lower base price, lease costs, financing or include packages for free
drafts.description: Customers request lower base price (< $50,000), cheaper lease than competitor, free inclusion of option packages, comfort package 30% discount, dealer margin reductions, and 0% financing—these are price/finance requests.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: All pricing, dealer margin and financing requests are noted for commercial/pricing teams; not handled as product feature requirements.
drafts.scope_reason: Price, lease, discount and financing requests are commercial/pricing matters and therefore out of scope for product requirements. If a product outcome is desired (for example bundling an item into a package), that is covered separately.
